correctness.rationale: For a zero \(a_i\), the Italian condition is exactly \(W_B-f(b_i)\ge2\), and symmetrically for a zero \(b_i\). These identities yield the lower bounds and reduce every weight-four optimum for \(n\ge4\) to side weights \(2,2\), except the two all-one-side functions when \(n=4\). At side weight \(2\), a zero on one side forces the matched opposite label to be zero, so the two nonzero index supports coincide; the only possible common supports have size one with two labels \(2\), or size two with four labels \(1\). The proof handles all \(n\ge3\), and `verify.py` independently checks every labeling of total weight at most \(4\) for \(3\le n\le12\).

value.rationale: The crown graph is the canonical one-factor deletion of \(K_{n,n}\). Italian domination is sensitive to exactly this local deletion because a zero vertex loses the contribution of its matched opposite vertex. The result gives a complete natural classification of all optimal allocations, not just the scalar minimum, and isolates the support-alignment mechanism created by the missing perfect matching. This is a motivated structural boundary comparison with the complete bipartite case rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
